reuse.why: Introduces getExpectedScheduleAmount on top of the existing getApproxNumberThreshold and makes the pre-existing getScheduledAmount delegate to it, so every server, preview and UI consumer shares one rule.

duplication.why: All five inline midpoint calculations (schedule-template, forecast, updateActions, postTransactionForSchedule, preview) are replaced by calls to the one definition; nothing is restated.

placement.why: The rule lives in shared/schedules.ts beside getScheduledAmount; the API field is computed in scheduleModel.toExternal.

scope.why: Focused on the requested steps; routing getScheduledAmount through the new rule also changes UI display amounts, which is consistent with the request but not called out, and the stepwise release notes now partly contradict each other.

maintainability.why: One small, documented definition with a thin sign-inverting wrapper; the only wrinkle is two public entry points (getScheduledAmount with op vs getExpectedScheduleAmount) for the same rule.

bypasses_abstraction.where: Every site that needs the expected amount calls getExpectedScheduleAmount or getScheduledAmount, which delegates to it.

disguised_duplication.where: getScheduledAmount delegates instead of keeping its own range logic; no reshaped copies remain.

abstraction_drift.where: getScheduledAmount gains an op parameter that it only forwards to getExpectedScheduleAmount; no special-case branches or bypassing call sites.
